data.title: Tinea pedis & onychomycosis — viva
data.summary: Fungal infections · 8 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Tinea pedis & onychomycosis** (Fungal infections)_

**Q1. Types of tinea pedis?**
- Interdigital (commonest, 4th web space — maceration, fissuring)
- Moccasin/chronic hyperkeratotic (T. rubrum — diffuse plantar scaling)
- Vesiculobullous (T. mentagrophytes — instep)
- Acute ulcerative (with Gram-negative superinfection)

**Q2. What is 'two feet–one hand' syndrome?**
- Bilateral tinea pedis with unilateral tinea manuum (usually dominant/scratching hand) — T. rubrum

**Q3. What is an id (dermatophytid) reaction?**
- Sterile vesicular eruption on palms/fingers as an allergic reaction to an active fungal infection elsewhere (often inflammatory tinea pedis); KOH-negative; clears when infection is treated

**Q4. Clinical types of onychomycosis?**
- Distal and lateral subungual (commonest), superficial white (T. mentagrophytes/moulds), proximal subungual (T. rubrum — suspect HIV), endonyx, total dystrophic, candidal (paronychia, onycholysis), mixed

**Q5. Differential diagnosis of onychomycosis?**
- Nail psoriasis (pits, oil-drop), lichen planus (pterygium), trauma/onycholysis, yellow nail syndrome, pachyonychia, eczema nail changes, subungual tumours, onychogryphosis

**Q6. Investigations?**
- KOH with nail clippings from proximal edge of onycholysis, culture (dermatophyte vs non-dermatophyte mould — repeat culture), nail clipping histopathology with PAS (most sensitive), dermoscopy (jagged proximal edge, spikes, longitudinal striae), PCR

**Q7. Treatment of onychomycosis?**
- Topical (≤50% nail, no matrix): amorolfine 5% lacquer weekly, ciclopirox 8% daily, efinaconazole/tavaborole
- Systemic: terbinafine 250 mg/day — 6 weeks fingernails, 12 weeks toenails (drug of choice for dermatophytes); itraconazole pulse 200 mg twice daily 1 week/month (2 pulses fingers, 3 toes) — also covers Candida/moulds; fluconazole weekly
- Adjuncts: chemical (40% urea) or surgical avulsion, debridement, lasers; combination improves cure

**Q8. Prevention of tinea pedis?**
- Dry toe webs, absorbent socks, antifungal powder, open/breathable footwear, avoid barefoot in communal showers, treat household members

## Quick spotter facts
- Thickened yellow crumbling toenails with subungual debris — distal lateral subungual onychomycosis

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Superficial fungal infection — tinea pedis, tinea unguium); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.18 and ch.58. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
